speaker: narrator
text: The Lantern and Bell is the only inn at the crossroads. Low beams, a roaring fire, garlic over every window.

speaker: hanne
text: Sit by the fire, loves. Nobody comes to Vellmoor this late in the year on purpose.

speaker: narrator
text: You lay the letter on the table. Hanne reads the name, and her face goes still.

speaker: hanne
text: That's not Anton's hand. Anton wrote like a clerk. And Anton Morosz died at dusk, at his daughter's door.

speaker: hanne
text: There were others like you, once. Sister Agnes keeps the church.

speaker: hanne
text: The apothecary's boy, Emeric, haunts the market. Wren Kessel digs graves over the hill.

speaker: hanne
text: Find them, if you mean to stay. And you will stay. Nobody leaves Vellmoor now. Not since spring.

speaker: hanne
text: Go up the hill to the burgomaster's house. His girl is still there. For now.

speaker: narrator
text: A tall stone house on the hill road, black crepe on the door. Anton Morosz kept the valley's ledgers for thirty years.

speaker: narrator
text: He found his daughter on the church step as a baby. When the mist came, he stood at her door with a poker, and stayed.

speaker: anton
text: You will not have her. Not while I'm in this house.

speaker: narrator
text: His son Andrei meets you on the stair, still in his shirtsleeves. He has not slept.

speaker: andrei
text: Father wrote no letter. But you came, so stay. Keep my sister. I can't, not against that.

speaker: narrator
text: On the sill of her room, a pressed mountain violet. Mountain violets do not grow in the valley.

speaker: narrator
text: On her dresser, a letter on cream paper, in the same old hand as yours. Come home, it says. You have been away so long.

speaker: narrator
text: Lenka comes down in her mourning black, her father's seal ring on a cord at her neck.

speaker: lenka
text: He has written to me since spring. I burned every letter. They kept coming. I won't sit in this house and wait for him.

speaker: lenka
text: I'm coming with you. Choose which of you I walk beside.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside, the light is going. On the road below, the wolves have begun to gather.

speaker: narrator
text: The soil around Father Oskar's grave is heaped outward, in a ring. Whatever left the coffin did not need a spade.

speaker: wren
text: Dug from the inside. Fingers, not claws. He was a tidy man. He folded the shroud.

speaker: narrator
text: In the vestry, letters in Oskar's hand, four lines in four margins, as if he knew he would not finish.

speaker: narrator
text: He keeps the faith of the dead. He rests where the guard once stood.

speaker: narrator
text: He lies beneath what was dug. He sleeps in the name of the first.

speaker: narrator
text: Someone is standing in the next row of graves, in a priest's cassock gone black with earth.

speaker: oskar
text: You came. I asked so many, and you are the ones who came. He will call her by another name. Don't let her answer.

speaker: narrator
text: The priest's gentle face splits into hunger, and he comes for the living.

speaker: narrator
text: Oskar lies down in his own grave again, and this time he stays. Someone should say the words.

speaker: narrator
text: You hold the churchyard gate shut while it shakes, and bar it, and it costs you blood. Behind it, he is still standing.

speaker: narrator
text: In the last letter, a line underscored twice: the bookkeeper knows every door in that castle. Ask him what he sold.

speaker: narrator
text: In the last letter, a line underscored twice: the son has been seen on the hill road after dark. Ask him why.

speaker: narrator
text: In the last letter, a line underscored twice: the girl who pours his wine still comes down to the village. For whom?

speaker: narrator
text: Somewhere in the village the bell begins to ring, and nobody is pulling the rope.

speaker: narrator
text: Old Berta came into the valley before the mist, and could not leave after. She has read cards for every burgomaster.

speaker: vadoma
text: Sit down. I have been expecting you since spring. Cut the cards. He is listening.

speaker: vadoma
text: A sword that was a brother's. It still remembers the sun. Look for it where the board shows you.

speaker: vadoma
text: A saint's light, carried out of a burning house and lost among the dead. It is waiting to be carried again.

speaker: vadoma
text: His own book, in his own hand. Do not open it until you hold the other two.

speaker: vadoma
text: He waits below, among his fathers. Where the dead of his house are kept.

speaker: vadoma
text: He waits where he prays, though he has nothing left to pray to.

speaker: vadoma
text: He waits high up, where the guard once stood watch over the valley.

speaker: vadoma
text: He waits among his letters, at the desk where he writes in that fine old hand.

speaker: vadoma
text: He wants a seat at your table. Count the chairs.

speaker: vadoma
text: He wants her to open the last door herself.

speaker: vadoma
text: He wants a brother's grief buried again.

speaker: vadoma
text: He wants the whole valley on its knees.

speaker: emeric
text: Is that a metaphor? Please tell me that's a metaphor.

speaker: vadoma
text: Everything is a metaphor, little scholar, until it bites you.

speaker: narrator
text: The sun comes up grey and warms nothing. On the hill, a door opens. He is walking now.

speaker: narrator
text: Down the last stair, in a lead-lined chest, the rotted cloth falls away. The blade gives light, though no candle burns.

speaker: narrator
text: There is a name cut into the cross-guard. Stefan.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside, the wolves stop all at once. A tall shape stands in the doorway, black against the mist.

speaker: count
text: Listen to them, the children of the dark. What music they make!

speaker: narrator
text: The light in the blade turns gold, and the shape in the doorway steps back, once, as a man steps back from a fire.

speaker: count
text: Put that down. It was never yours. It was never anyone's but his.

speaker: narrator
text: Then the doorway is empty, and the wolves begin again.

speaker: narrator
text: The blade keeps its light all the way to the road. Something on four legs follows at a distance, and does not catch up.

speaker: narrator
text: A stair goes down further than the hill is tall. Behind you, the wall closes like a mouth.

speaker: narrator
text: The bones in the walls are not where they were. Every time you look back, the passage behind you is a different shape.

speaker: narrator
text: At the bottom, in a niche, a small silver lamp. Its flame burns white and does not move in the draught.

speaker: agnes
text: Saint Ysolde. I carried you out of the fire. I lost you on the road. Forgive me.

speaker: narrator
text: As you lift it, the flame leans toward you, the way a dog leans toward its owner.

speaker: narrator
text: On the way up, an empty coffin stands on the stair, fresh earth on its lid.

speaker: narrator
text: Whatever lay in it has gone up to the castle, wearing someone's face.

speaker: narrator
text: You climb into the air. It is the first time any of you has been glad of the mist.

speaker: narrator
text: Vellmoor buries its burgomaster without a priest. Hanne reads the words, badly, from Oskar's book.

speaker: narrator
text: Beside Anton lies a second coffin. Dorka Halasz, nineteen, in her wedding dress.

speaker: narrator
text: Her mother said she had waited long enough.

speaker: narrator
text: She went up the hill alone, the week before you came. She meant to offer herself, if he would leave her friend alone.

speaker: lenka
text: She never told me. She just went. He found me on the church step, and now I'm putting him in the ground beside it.

speaker: narrator
text: The lid of the second coffin is not nailed. Every candle in the church leans toward it.

speaker: narrator
text: The hammer is very loud in the little church. Her mother does not scream. She just stops breathing for a while.

speaker: narrator
text: Under the nails, something knocks, once, and then is still.

speaker: narrator
text: Her mother pulls one bent nail from the lid and presses it into your hand. Keep it. It held her.

speaker: narrator
text: You wait, to be sure. Nobody looks away from the coffin, so nobody sees the candles go out along the back wall.

speaker: narrator
text: Then Dorka Halasz sits up in her wedding dress, and it is the sweetest smile anyone in the room has ever seen.

speaker: dorka
text: Come to me. Leave these others and come to me. He's so kind. He's so patient. He'll wait for her as long as it takes.

speaker: narrator
text: When it is done, Dorka is only a girl in a wedding dress again, with a peace on her face she did not have a minute ago.

speaker: lenka
text: You stayed to the end. Not everyone stays, for me.

speaker: narrator
text: They bury Anton Morosz at dawn, properly. On the lid, someone has left a pressed violet. No one saw who.

speaker: narrator
text: Jakob Brenner kept the castle's books for twenty years.

speaker: narrator
text: Then one spring he walked down the hill and asked to be locked up, for safety. Whose safety, he would not say.

speaker: jakob
text: Visitors! The blood is the life, friends. Flies are only a little life. One must start small.

speaker: jakob
text: You want to know where his earth went. I wrote the shipping orders. Plans cost. Debit, credit.

speaker: jakob
text: Something that matters. A drop of your blood on my tongue, or a thing you carry that he fears.

speaker: jakob
text: Oh, he does like you. I can taste it. Debit.

speaker: jakob
text: He'll hate that I have this. Lovely. Debit.

speaker: jakob
text: Three boxes, in the last parish. One under the chapel, two on the village carts. He sleeps in one, turn and turn about.

speaker: jakob
text: He sleeps in boxes. That's all you get for nothing. Credit nothing, debit nothing.

speaker: jakob
text: Who let him in? Not me. I only kept the books. The books never open a door.

speaker: jakob
text: Ask the burgomaster's boy where he walks at dusk. The Master pays well for a son's grief.

speaker: jakob
text: The little maid pours his wine and counts his glasses. She counts other things too.

speaker: jakob
text: I don't want to talk to you. You don't count now. The Master is at hand.

speaker: narrator
text: Behind you, the cell fills with flies again, and Jakob is singing a counting song under his breath.

speaker: narrator
text: The mist is so thick now that noon looks like evening.

speaker: narrator
text: Long boxes of black earth, nailed shut, stencilled in a neat ledger hand. Garden soil. Handle with care.

speaker: emeric
text: Grave earth, but not this valley's. They must rest in their own earth, or not at all.

speaker: narrator
text: The earth burns like peat. Somewhere up on the hill, someone feels it.

speaker: narrator
text: This box screams as it burns. Not the wood. The earth.

speaker: narrator
text: The last box goes up in one breath. On the hill, for the first time in a generation, a castle window goes dark.

speaker: narrator
text: By the village carts, a girl in a maid's apron and faded castle livery watches you burn his earth. She doesn't stop you.

speaker: marta
text: I pour his wine. I've poured it for years. I still come home at dusk, when he lets me. Whose side does that put me on?

speaker: count
text: You think to baffle me, with your pale faces all in a row, like sheep in a butcher's.

speaker: narrator
text: On the bottom of a box lid, an order slip: one extra box, sent to the lockhouse, signed J.B.

speaker: narrator
text: On the bottom of a box lid, an order slip: delivered by the burgomaster's own cart. Received by the son.

speaker: narrator
text: On the bottom of a box lid, an order slip: delivered by the little gate. Opened by M.

speaker: narrator
text: Wherever he lies now, he lies uneasy.

speaker: narrator
text: A heavy book in faded green leather, clasped with a brass lock shaped like a closed eye.

speaker: narrator
text: The lock opens before anyone touches it. He wants this read.

speaker: narrator
text: I, Vlad, first son of this house, set down how I lost my soul, so whoever reads may know it was not taken. I gave it.

speaker: narrator
text: I loved Ludmila of the high meadow. She loved my brother Stefan.

speaker: narrator
text: On their wedding day I made a bargain, and killed my brother with his own sword.

speaker: ludmila
text: I will open the window, but not for him. If I come again, I will choose again, and it will not be you.

speaker: narrator
text: The last page is fresh ink. She has come again, in the burgomaster's house. Ludmila's soul. Lenka's face. She says no.

speaker: narrator
text: And beneath it, his plan. One of them will wear my mark and sit at their table, and they will not know until it is done.

speaker: narrator
text: And beneath it, his plan. She will turn from them, a step at a time, until she opens the last door herself.

speaker: narrator
text: And beneath it, his plan. My brother's blade will grow dull in their hands, until it cannot finish what she begins.

speaker: narrator
text: And beneath it, his plan. House by house, the valley will go dark, until there is no one left to say no.

speaker: lenka
text: My name is Lenka Morosz. I am not her. And if I were, I would still say no.

speaker: count
text: Your girls that you all love are mine already. Come up the hill, and see.

speaker: narrator
text: Dawn does not come. Only a greyness, and the castle above it, every window lit.

speaker: narrator
text: In the grey before dawn, a pressed violet on the sill where Lenka slept. The shutters were barred till dawn.

speaker: narrator
text: A violet under Lenka's pillow, flat as paper, its stem tied with one gold thread from a wedding veil.

speaker: narrator
text: A violet on the step where Lenka slept, wrapped in a scrap of painted canvas. Someone has been painting her.

speaker: lenka
text: Another one. He wants me to know he can reach the window. He wants you to know it too.

speaker: narrator
text: At the twelfth stroke the dead come walking.

speaker: narrator
text: Every hunter who ever climbed that hill is in the line. They do not stop. One of them does.

speaker: ursula
text: Sister Agnes kept my infirmary after me, and kept it badly. Tell her I am not angry. Tell her to come and ask me why.

speaker: jozef
text: Tell Wren Kessel it was the right stake. She did right by her father. Tell her there is more, if she will walk with me.

speaker: gerhardt
text: Tell the apothecary's boy his page one was wrong. The affliction is not sent. It is invited.

speaker: narrator
text: You step into the line beside the ghost, and walk a while with the dead. You step out knowing something you did not.

speaker: narrator
text: You turn away. The ghost bows, and leaves a vial of water on the step, cold enough to ring.

speaker: narrator
text: The line walks on toward the castle. By morning there may be one more lantern in it, unless you are careful.

speaker: narrator
text: Three objects. A brother's blade, a saint's light, and his own book. The castle road is the only road left in Vellmoor.

speaker: narrator
text: A chasm with no bottom, and across it the drawbridge, raised. Along the wall, a little side gate the servants used.

speaker: count
text: Welcome to my house! Enter freely and of your own will!

speaker: marta
text: Marta. I pour his wine up there. I'll open the little gate, if you ask. It's the slow way, but he never watches it.

speaker: lenka
text: And don't you dare leave me at the bottom of the hill. I'm coming up with you.

speaker: narrator
text: The drawbridge comes down, slow as a held breath. You walk in by the front door, as guests.

speaker: narrator
text: Above you, something on the battlements turns its head.

speaker: narrator
text: Someone inside works the chains. The drawbridge comes down without a sound. Nothing on the battlements turns its head.

speaker: narrator
text: You go the long way, along the lip of the chasm, the way the servant girls once left. It costs you.

speaker: narrator
text: But nothing on the battlements turns its head.

speaker: narrator
text: Not yet. You turn back down the road. The castle will wait. It has always waited.

speaker: narrator
text: A long gallery of the house's portraits. The eyes follow you. That is ordinary. What is not ordinary is that some blink.

speaker: emeric
text: Same face. Four hundred years of fashions, and the same face. That's not a family. That's a man.

speaker: narrator
text: One painted lord holds your eyes and will not let go. The longer you look, the harder it is to remember why you came.

speaker: narrator
text: You tear your eyes away, and it costs you. The painted lord smiles and lets you pass.

speaker: narrator
text: You throw a cloth over the frame. Under it, something knocks, once, and is still.

speaker: narrator
text: At the end of the gallery hangs one canvas under a cloth that has never been lifted. You leave it be.

speaker: narrator
text: The wall turns. A stair goes up into the dark.

speaker: narrator
text: His family's crypt, under everything. Every coffin is open but one. He stands beside it, old, and very tall.

speaker: narrator
text: A small cold chapel, its window bricked shut. Fresh violets on the altar. He kneels there, old, and rises as you enter.

speaker: narrator
text: The top of the highest tower, open to the wind, where the guard once stood.

speaker: narrator
text: The valley lies under the mist below. He waits at the edge, old, and patient.

speaker: narrator
text: A study lined with letters, every one in the same fine old hand. The hand that wrote to you. He sets down his pen.

speaker: count
text: You have come a long way to be refused. I know the feeling.

speaker: narrator
text: He moves faster than an old man should, and the cold comes with him.

speaker: lenka
text: My name is Lenka Morosz. I am not her. And if I were, I would say what she said. No.

speaker: narrator
text: The Lantern's light goes into the dark where he kept her, and she walks out of it on her own.

speaker: narrator
text: Stefan's blade finds his heart, and for the first time in four hundred years he looks surprised.

speaker: narrator
text: You fall back down the stair. He does not follow. He has time, and he knows you will come back.
